Caerulomycin K is implicated in targeting the Mcl-1 protein, which is known to play a critical role in myeloid cell differentiation and survival. Mcl-1 is a key regulator of apoptosis and is often upregulated in cancer cells, making it a promising target for therapeutic intervention. The (6aR,11aR)-9-hydroxy-3-methoxy-6a,11a-dihydro-6H-[1]benzofuro[3,2-c]chromene-2-carbaldehyde, which is a known inhibitor of Mcl-1, is shown to have a target of the EDD domain protein, DegV family. This indicates that the EDD domain protein, DegV family, may be a downstream effector of the Mcl-1 pathway, potentially involved in cellular processes that are modulated by Caerulomycin K. The evidence suggests a possible regulatory pathway where Caerulomycin K may influence Mcl-1 activity, which in turn affects the EDD domain protein, DegV family. The strength of the evidence is moderate, as it is based on a single interaction, and further experimental validation would be necessary to confirm the direct relationship between Caerulomycin K and the EDD domain protein, DegV family.
